responsibility: This is the main driver for GCC’s LTO front end. It orchestrates the three execution modes—full LTO, whole-program analysis (WPA), and local transformation (LTRANS)—by initializing the LTO reader, loading symbol and callgraph data, materializing function bodies when needed, running WPA IPA analysis and partitioning, streaming partition outputs, handling parallel partition emission/jobserver interaction, promoting statics in non-WPA flows, and finally handing the unified symtab to the normal middle-end compilation pipeline.
same_name_distinction: This is the top-level driver for the module: it runs LTO/WPA/LTRANS workflows, materializes bodies, invokes partitioning, and streams partitions out. In contrast, gcc/lto/lto.h is the module-wide header that defines shared LTO data structures and declares cross-file APIs such as object-section and entry-point interfaces.
